modelCard.what: An early, experimental simulation of NFL preseason games. It runs 10,000 game simulations and reports the range of scores it sees.
modelCard.honestLimit: Tested on a full held-out preseason, this model picked winners no better than a coin flip. Its win percentages are therefore deliberately pulled close to 50% — the widest it will ever go is 45.3%–50.6%.
modelCard.whatItIsGoodFor: Seeing a plausible score range and how it compares with the sportsbook market. It is not a betting recommendation and has not been shown to beat the market.
modelCard.whyPublishItAtAll: Publishing it with its results tracked is how it earns — or fails to earn — a stronger status over time.

teamSignal.note: This model has no measurable read on which of these two teams is better in preseason: the coefficient linking team strength to margin is indistinguishable from zero (t = -0.5746, 95% interval [-0.077667,0.042782]). Rather than publish a direction it cannot support, the team term is set to zero, so this forecast reflects preseason scoring and home context only.

winProbability.calibration: Shrunk toward 50% by a factor fit before testing (λ=0.25).

marketComparison.note: The sportsbook numbers are the books' own, shown for context. A difference is a difference — this model has not been shown to beat the market.

forecasts.disclaimer: Experimental preseason model. Educational and paper-only — not betting advice, and not shown to beat the market.
